categories.main_business_segments: Nutanix operates as a single business segment focused on providing a unified software platform for hybrid multicloud computing. The company delivers solutions that enable organizations to run applications and manage data across private data centers, public clouds, and edge locations, supporting a wide range of workloads and industries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Nutanix's core technologies include its Nutanix Cloud Platform, which is built on hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) that merges compute, storage, and networking into a software-defined platform. Key products and technologies include Nutanix AOS (scale-out storage), AHV (native hypervisor), Data Services for Kubernetes, Flow Network Security, Prism management, and unified storage solutions. The company leverages a software-centric approach, running on commodity x86 servers and integrating with major public clouds and external storage providers.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Nutanix serves a diverse customer base of over 29,000 end customers across industries such as financial services, retail, manufacturing, public sector, automotive, consumer goods, education, energy, healthcare, media, technology, and telecommunications. The company also sells to service providers who use its platform to deliver cloud-based services to their own customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Nutanix operates globally with significant presence in North America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA), Asia Pacific, and Latin America. In fiscal 2025, approximately 44% of revenue was derived from international customers, and the company maintains offices and R&D centers worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Nutanix is positioned as a software platform provider in the IT infrastructure supply chain, operating downstream from hardware manufacturers and OEMs. The company does not manufacture hardware itself but partners with OEMs and relies on contract manufacturers for its branded hardware, focusing primarily on software development, integration, and support.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Nutanix's strategic focus is on expanding its hybrid multicloud and AI-ready platform capabilities, deepening ecosystem and partner integrations, and driving innovation in areas such as Kubernetes management, data services, and enterprise AI. The company invests heavily in R&D to enhance its platform, support new workloads (including AI and cloud-native applications), and enable consistent operations across diverse environments. Project Beacon exemplifies its multi-year effort to deliver data-centric platform services across clouds.
categories.revenue_model: Nutanix operates a subscription-based revenue model, selling term-based software licenses and SaaS offerings with durations typically ranging from one to five years. Revenue is generated from software subscriptions (recognized both upfront and ratably), support and entitlements, and professional services. The majority of sales are made through channel partners and OEMs.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Nutanix competes in the highly competitive cloud infrastructure and platform services market against software providers like VMware by Broadcom, Microsoft, and Red Hat; public cloud providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud; and traditional IT vendors including Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Pure Storage. The company positions itself as a leader in hybrid multicloud and HCI, emphasizing openness, flexibility, and customer choice.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2025, Nutanix reported total revenue of $2.54 billion, representing 18% year-over-year growth. The company achieved GAAP net income of $188 million and ended the year with over 29,000 customers. Gross margin improved to 86.8%, and annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $2.22 billion, reflecting strong growth and a transition to sustained profitability.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Nutanix differentiates itself by offering a unified, open, and secure hybrid multicloud platform that simplifies IT operations, supports a broad range of workloads (including AI and cloud-native applications), and provides freedom of choice across hardware, storage, and cloud environments. Its platform emphasizes ease of use, scalability, integrated data services, and seamless management across on-premises and public clouds, enabling customers to accelerate innovation and reduce complexity.
